binding_interpretation: G1 permits necessary, tightly coupled product jobs supported by host-system demand; it does not require a purchase order for a future startup product. G7 requires two independent timing sources including one primary or official 2028-2035 trigger.

G1.rationale: Pattern Energy documents a funded-developer 525 kV VSC-HVDC project with a converter station and 2029-2032 schedule. DOE independently directs industry to standardize HVDC requirements by 2030 and establish national HVDC testing/certification during 2030-2040. Wideband current/voltage measurement is a necessary closed-loop protection, control, and certification job inside every VSC converter station, supported by the accepted technical records; the proposed hybrid sensor socket remains uncontracted and therefore marginal.

G4.rationale: LEM, optical-current-transformer vendors, and China incumbents are named. A single platform combining DC accuracy, protection bandwidth, calibrated digital outputs, and converter-certification traceability is non-cosmetic, but the claimed performance must be benchmarked against those incumbents.

G6.rationale: The base case is domestic US HVDC and industrial deployment; China is not claimed. Normal grid-equipment safety, EMC, calibration, cybersecurity, and restricted-party screening remain in the qualification plan.

G7.rationale: The company path retains the bounded 2026-2029 sensor benchmark. Pattern names full construction in 2029 and in-service in 2032 for an exact VSC-HVDC converter project; DOE independently names 2025-2030 standardization and a 2030-2040 national HVDC test/certification center. The window is real but incumbent converter OEMs may bundle sensing before a 2030 entrant qualifies.
